assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clearly identifiable discovery: a high-mobility two-dimensional electron system at the polar/non-polar LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface, followed by emergent superconductivity, magnetism and gate-tunable phases. It opened oxide-interface electronics as a field and sits close to my own work on oxide interfaces, oxygen vacancies and atomic-scale interface structure, so I judge both its importance and its experimental subtleties from direct experience.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 observation of the interfacial conducting layer is credited to Ohtomo and Hwang. Mannhart's group contributed the electric-field tunability and the superconducting phase, with Triscone and collaborators, so the third place is arguable. The decisive credit is Ohtomo and Hwang, with Mannhart as the most defensible third.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide for over twenty years. The electronic reconstruction picture has been refined, and the roles of oxygen vacancies and cation intermixing remain debated. The central discovery is robust, but the mechanism of the carriers is not fully closed.
uncertainties: Polar-catastrophe versus defect or intermixing origin of the carriers is still discussed; microscopy shows interface intermixing that complicates a clean picture.
Whether the third credit belongs to Mannhart or to others with the superconductivity and tunability results (for example Triscone, not in the credited names) is unresolved.
Application impact is limited so far, so the case rests on fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the 2018 observation of correlated-insulator and superconducting states opened moire quantum materials. It is a new, tunable platform for correlated physics with very wide follow-up, and the discovery is concrete and teachable.
assessment.attribution: Theory credit is Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011), and the experimental discovery is Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (Cao et al., 2018). That pairing of theory and experiment gives a natural configuration. First-author experimentalists and others, such as Yuan Cao, are not creditable under the supplied names, which I flag.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups, and the field is very active. The interpretation of the superconductivity is not settled, and the field is still young, so recognition might be somewhat early but not premature given the breadth of confirmation.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Sample inhomogeneity and twist-angle disorder complicate comparison between devices.
Whether a prize in this area should wait for the fractional and zero-field phases to mature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and realization of topological insulators, from the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells to the quantized anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators, changed how band topology is understood and observed. It is one of the major conceptual advances in condensed matter in this century, and the surface and edge states are probed directly by spectroscopy and microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the key Z2 theory, and Molenkamp's group first observed the edge-state transport in 2007 following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Xue's group made the first quantum anomalous Hall observation in 2013. This candidate mixes several sub-results, and Mele, Bernevig and Zhang are not available in this entry, so the configuration is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently confirmed, with extensive follow-up in materials and devices. It is mature for recognition. The quantization precision and applications are still developing.
uncertainties: The compound nature means the prize would need to decide between the Z2 theory, the HgTe experiment, and the QAH realisation.
Omitted contributors with strong claims, notably Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and Mele, cannot be proposed from this entry.
I am relying on memory of the literature and have not verified the details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and later giant TMR in MgO barrier junctions, is a clear discovery with large technological impact in read heads and magnetic memory. It follows naturally from giant magnetoresistance (2007 prize) and relies on spin-dependent tunnelling through carefully engineered thin-film interfaces, which I appreciate from a materials and interface standpoint.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, independently. Parkin and, separately, Yuasa and collaborators realised the large coherent-tunnelling MgO effect in 2004, following Butler and Mathon theory. The supplied names support a fair configuration but omit Yuasa and the theorists.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and in widespread use for two decades. Timing is mature, but the case partly overlaps the earlier GMR prize and could be seen as incremental.
uncertainties: Credit for MgO giant TMR is shared with Yuasa and others not in the credited names.
Whether the committee sees it as sufficiently distinct from the GMR prize.
Independent discovery in 1995 raises the question of whether priority is balanced.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength idea and developed by Ye into instruments at the 10^-18 level, are a precision measurement achievement with clear impact on timekeeping, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The invention is crisp and the performance claims are checkable.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2001-2003), and Ye's group delivered record accuracy and stability. Other groups (for example Lemke, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom and colleagues at NIST, and Strontium and Ytterbium efforts in Europe) contributed. Two names give a clean allocation of credit for the concept and the leading realisation.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by multiple laboratories at a similar level, with international comparison and continued improvement. A redefinition of the second is under discussion but not required for the physics to be mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views optical clocks as a continuation of the 2005 and 2012 precision-measurement prizes.
Other groups with strong claims are not in the credited names.
The redefinition of the SI second is pending and not a criterion, but may shape timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental discovery of the skyrmion lattice in chiral magnets, with real-space imaging by Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, and the emergent electromagnetic response, introduced topological spin textures as a field. As a microscopist I note that direct real-space imaging was decisive for the acceptance of the interpretation.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer and colleagues identified the skyrmion lattice in MnSi by neutron scattering (2009), and Tokura's group imaged skyrmions in real space (2010) and extended the materials. Theoretical prediction by Bogdanov and coworkers, and the emergent-field theory, are not credited here, which weakens the fairness of a two-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed, and the field continues with room-temperature skyrmions. The device-level applications, such as racetrack memory, have not yet matured.
uncertainties: The role of the earlier theory by Bogdanov and others is not supported by the credited names.
Practical impact is still prospective.
Whether neutron and microscopy experiments should be recognised jointly or one preferred.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and rests on the conception and construction of two enormous detectors. The importance is unquestionable, and the 2013 prize recognised the theory but not the experimental side.
assessment.attribution: The statutes limit the prize to three persons, and the credit here goes to the founders and leaders of ATLAS and CMS. This is a delicate allocation, since thousands of physicists built the experiments and discovery. The proposed three are defensible as conceivers and spokespersons but the assignment will be contested; the committee must decide whether to honour leadership of the projects or the discovery itself.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: independently confirmed by two experiments, with couplings measured in the following run. Recognition is long past due, which may argue for urgency or may suggest the opportunity was missed.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit within large collaborations is intrinsically unresolved.
Whether the prize honours the discovery or the detector concept, and who among the many leaders is decisive.
The profile of the statutes versus the collaborative reality means a fair three-person configuration is hard to establish.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The titanium-sapphire laser and passive mode locking created the practical femtosecond laser used across spectroscopy, microscopy and ultrafast science, and attosecond methods, which I mentioned as Chair in 2023, build directly on this technology. The inventions are clear and enabling.
assessment.attribution: Moulton made the Ti:sapphire gain medium (1982), Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking (with Spence and Kean, 1991), and Keller introduced the semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM). The three-name configuration maps onto three distinct inventions, though other contributors such as Spence and Kean are omitted.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and ubiquitous. The risk is that ultrafast optics has recently been recognised (chirped pulse amplification in 2018 and attosecond physics in 2023), so the added increment might be judged smaller.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2018 and 2023 prizes may reduce its priority.
Other contributors to Kerr-lens mode locking are outside the credited names.
I have not verified the historical priority details independently.
